decoded.bearing-on-the-2026-09-21-records: nine records filed here on 2026-09-21 name BENrLoUb... as this surface's Solana payTo, and the 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-29 readings both read 5yASLjtNss... there. This measurement does not settle which is right. What it establishes is about today: the recipient is not minted per request on this surface now, so a reader cannot explain the difference by rotation between calls as it behaves today. It does not establish how the surface behaved on 2026-09-21: that pass archived no bytes, and three requests in six seconds a week later cannot rule out that the address rotated then. Separately, an address that an unrelated vendor presents as a fee payer is a poor candidate for this vendor's recipient, which is a reason and not a proof

finding: Three unpaid requests to one priced Bitrefill route, three seconds apart on 2026-09-29, returned identical recipients: one EVM address on Base, Arbitrum and Polygon and one Solana address, with the Solana entry's extra.feePayer the same in all three. This surface does not mint a recipient per request today. In the minute before, an unrelated vendor's priced endpoint (agents.allium.so) presented the same Solana fee payer while rotating its own Solana recipient on every request; all three Bitrefill readings and two of the three Allium ones are in this record's artifact, the third in the Allium transcript it names. A value two unrelated vendors' challenges share is consistent with settlement infrastructure they have in common, and who controls it was not established. This is filed against the open disagreement in the Bitrefill entry, where this registry's 2026-09-21 records name that fee payer as this surface's payTo. It does not settle it and cannot: the 2026-09-21 pass archived no bytes, and stability across three requests today says nothing about how the surface behaved a week ago. No payment was made; one IP is one sample.
